item.title: 3rd City Rangers donate K40, 000 to URP
item.description: (L-R) Tabe Jugari- Patron and Sponsor of 03rd City Rangers and Principal of Stout Lawyers donating the K40,000 to Hagen Open MP and United Resources Party (URP) Leader William Duma witnessed by Cr. Samuel Maniat Ward 8 Councillor Hagen Urban LLG and Mosley Tika- Former Hagen Eagles player (Supplied) The 3rd City Rangers Rugby Football League Club in Mt Hagen has donated a total of K40,000 to the U
item.content:encoded:
(L-R) Tabe Jugari- Patron and Sponsor of 03rd City Rangers and Principal of Stout Lawyers donating the K40,000 to Hagen Open MP and United Resources Party (URP) Leader William Duma witnessed by Cr. Samuel Maniat Ward 8 Councillor Hagen Urban LLG and Mosley Tika- Former Hagen Eagles player (Supplied)

The 3rd City Rangers Rugby Football League Club in Mt Hagen has donated a total of K40,000 to the United Resources Party (URP) led by Hagen Open MP and party leader William Duma.

The donation was made jointly by the 03rd City Rangers and its patron and sponsor, Tabe Jugari, the principal of Stout Lawyers.

According to the club, K20,000 was contributed by the 03rd City Rangers, while another K20,000 was donated by Mr Jugari in his personal capacity as the club’s patron and sponsor.

The money was formally presented to URP Leader and Hagen Open MP William Duma in Port Moresby.

"The donation is a show of support for the URP and its leadership, particularly its vision for the development of Papua New Guinea, Mt Hagen and Western Highlands Province," said Stout Lawyers Principal Mr. Jugari.

Jugari stress the Rangers also believe in building a strong partnership with the party and supporting development that benefits young people.

Hagen Open MP, William Duma says this is the first time his party has received support of this kind from a sporting team.

"This is the very first of its kind for our Party to receive support from a sporting team.

"I have supported sports especially rugby league, for a longtime even before I entered politics and throughout my political career," MP Duma said.

He describes the donation as a significant show of confidence and trust from young people in Mt Hagen and says it reflects their belief in the URP's vision for practical and people-centred leadership.

Duma also commended the 03rd City Rangers for their discipline, unity and achievements.

"I commend 03rd City Rangers for their discipline, unity and outstanding achievement and I look forward to a continued partnership in promoting youth development, sport and nation building," added Duma.

The 03rd City Rangers represents Wards One to Eight of the Hagen Urban Local Level Government (LLG), as well as Hagen Rural LLG and Western Highlands Province.

The team recently competed in the Rigo Rice Cup 2026, where it was declared one of the dual winners.

item.title: K3 Billion in lost log export and income tax revenues
item.description: About 3-billion-kina is estimated to have been lost in export revenue and income tax between 2023-2025 in the country’s logging forestry sector. This was revealed through a study conducted by the community advocacy group ACT NOW which showed the cost of logs exported from PNG were much lower than its import cost in China.
item.content:encoded:
About 3-billion-kina is estimated to have been lost in export revenue and income tax between 2023-2025 in the country’s logging forestry sector.

This was revealed through a study conducted by the community advocacy group ACT NOW which showed the cost of logs exported from PNG were much lower than its import cost in China.

Campaign Manager Eddie Tanago said this is a serious issue that must be looked into immediately by the government and other relevant authorities.

“The government, the relevant authorities really need to pay attention to the alerts, the red flags that civil societies like us or any other concerned body because these are all very important issues to the country.

“We have been talking about issues of illegal laundering, illegal logging, issues of money laundering, issues of forest crime and yet, these are not acted on.

“The banking sector is involved as well to facilitate, to keep the accounts of those who are doing business, the real estate agents, the lawyers, the accountants. It is a whole heap of bodies that provides the conducive environment for such business to flourish,” Tanago said.

Similarly, a previous report released by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime from 2018 to 2022 revealed a discrepancy of over 6-billion-kina between export values from PNG and import values to China.

Mr Tanago said this trend over the past years without action by relevant government bodies is very concerning.

He said such dealings which may involve transfer pricing, tax evasion is closely linked to money laundering within the logging industry, and is straining the country’s economy, especially in this El Nino period when communities, schools and hospitals are in immense need of funding.

The Act NOW Campaign Manager is calling on the relevant stakeholders and banks to take corrective measures to immediately rectify and prevent other similar occurrences.

“We are all in an El Nino season and we are in dire need of funding. Our communities really need those monies. And we are talking about potential revenue for Papua New Guinea that is going down the drain.

“The call now is to, yes, the government, its relevant authorities, including sectors that play a key role in enabling such businesses to flourish. We need to act. Especially we need the government to really step up and push for this and the banks as well,” Tanago said.

PNG Forest Authority will be releasing a statement on this.

item.title: Mothers in Kundiawa receive free life skills training
item.description: Mothers from Ward 3 in Kundiawa Urban LLG celebrate after completing their life skills training and thank XSPI and PNG Working Group (NBC News) Twelve mothers in Ward 3 area in the Kundiawa Urban LLG are not the same after receiving free life skills training.
item.content:encoded:
Mothers from Ward 3 in Kundiawa Urban LLG celebrate after completing their life skills training and thank XSPI and PNG Working Group (NBC News)

Twelve mothers in Ward 3 area in the Kundiawa Urban LLG are not the same after receiving free life skills training.

The training was delivered under the Family Economic Empowerment program under the Drought Outreach Program, supported by XSPI of Australian NGO and PNG Working Group.

Livelihood specialist and lead trainer Agnes Siune said the skills will help mothers turn their staple food into flour and store it for future use when El Nino or disaster happens.

She said it will also pave the way for them to venture into markets, and to know how to make a balanced diet and cook using different recipes.

In a small but significant gathering, the mothers who attended the training left with something they did not have before — skills to feed their family and make money.

Ms Siune said she has trained more than 30 women in the six districts in Simbu, who have now become trainers and are training mothers in the villages of Simbu province.

She said mothers in the villages who have been trained are now making tapioca cake, sweet potato (kaukau) muffin, banana cake, cookies and organic spice and soup.

Apolonia Gena, a mother of six who attended the training, thanked lead trainer Agnes Siune for bringing the skills to the mothers.

She said this life skills training will stay with them forever.

"SME training takes forever without favorable outcome. Training we receive is simple, productive and will help us in many ways," she said.

Lucas Wamne said all mothers, especially housewives and young women who do nothing in the village or town, should gain such unique skills and venture into small market to sustain themselves.

Mothers from Ward 3 area in Kundiawa Urban LLG all urged the local-level and district development authority to assist them with locally made oven and hand grill to put into practice what they have learnt.

item.title: GPSH maintains operations despite El Nino and funding challenges
item.description: Goroka Provincial Specialist Hospital (GPSH) main entrance (NBC News) The Eastern Highlands Provincial Health Authority (EHPHA) has assured the public that Goroka Provincial Specialist Hospital (GPSH) continues to operate despite challenges affecting the delivery of healthcare services.
item.content:encoded:
Goroka Provincial Specialist Hospital (GPSH) main entrance (NBC News)

The Eastern Highlands Provincial Health Authority (EHPHA) has assured the public that Goroka Provincial Specialist Hospital (GPSH) continues to operate despite challenges affecting the delivery of healthcare services.

EHPHA Chief Executive Officer, Dr Pomuso Warima, has clarified the hospital's position following an earlier memo announcing a scale-down of operations due to challenges caused by El Niño, power disruptions and funding constraints.

In his updated response, Dr Warima assured the public that hospital services have not been closed and all operations are being maintained.

The ongoing El Niño conditions have severely affected power supply across the province, with reduced water levels at Yonki Dam forcing PNG Power to implement power rationing.

Warima said frequent power surges and outages have also damaged some expensive medical equipment, despite the hospital having Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) systems in place.

“The hospital is working to repair the damaged equipment and put measures in place to protect its medical assets.” He said.

CEO Warima said all hospital operations are being maintained, with priority given to emergency cases and essential services during the El Niño period.

“Our priority was, and remains, to scale up services, especially elective surgery and consultation clinics, as conditions improve. Any suggestion that services were closed is incorrect,” he said.

On funding, Dr Warima confirmed that EHPHA had not received its funding allocations for June, July and August, adding that budget cuts and delays in the release of funds by Treasury had placed further pressure on operations. “Despite this delay, we have money to keep us going,” he said.

He said the authority was relying on carefully maintained rollover funds to sustain hospital operations, including the purchase of essential medicines and medical consumables.

“This has allowed us to sustain operations without shutting down services,” Dr Warima said.

The main concern for EHPA is the increasing number of short-Term Contract Officers recruited due to acute manpower shortages costing the Provincial Authority to spend more.

CEO Warima further stated that the growing number of short-term contract officers recruited to address critical manpower shortages is placing additional financial pressure on the provincial health authority.

item.title: Kanga community in Kokoda embrace development
item.description: The people of Kanga in Ward One, Kokoda LLG, Sohe district will now have access to basic government services such as Health, Education and Small to Medium Enterprise activities. This follows the construction of a 5.5-kilometre road from Ebei to Kanga village — giving the people access to services they have lacked for the last 50 years.
item.content:encoded:
The people of Kanga in Ward One, Kokoda LLG, Sohe district will now have access to basic government services such as Health, Education and Small to Medium Enterprise activities.

This follows the construction of a 5.5-kilometre road from Ebei to Kanga village — giving the people access to services they have lacked for the last 50 years.

The people of Kanga initiated the 5.5-kilometre road project from Ebei to Kanga with their own funding of over K400,000, while the Sohe District Development Authority (DDA) co-funded the project with K800,000 to complete it.

An emotional Ward One councillor for Kokoda LLG, Gabriel Puni, said the road project marks a new era for his people of Kanga to access basic services.

“For far too long we have been seen as the backpage of Kokoda LLG in Sohe District, but this time we will have equal opportunity to basic services through this road project,” Mr Puni said.

Mr Puni thanked the Sohe DDA for stepping in and supporting their community-initiated project, saying it is the first of its kind in Sohe and Northern Province where a community like Kanga has come on board to fulfil a community-initiated project, especially to do with road.

Meanwhile, the construction of the 5.5-kilometre road from Ebei to Kanga was spearheaded by local Kanga contractor, R & B Construction Limited, with its partner contractor, Pangalio Construction Limited.

However, Ward One Councillor Gabriel Puni called on the Sohe District and Oro Provincial Government to counter-fund a bridge project for the Misanu River that flows between the newly constructed road. He said the bridge will help the people travel safely between Ebei and Kanga, rather than wet-crossing.

Mr Puni stressed that many Kanga people have lost their lives trying to cross the fast-flowing Misanu River over the last 50 years.

The newly constructed 5.5-kilometre road from Ebei to Kanga was officially opened by Sohe DDA Chairman and Member for Sohe, Henry Johns Amuli, and witnessed by delegates from the office of the Oro Provincial Government, Provincial Works, Sohe district, media, and the Ebei and Kanga communities.

item.title: Bialla police barracks commissioned
item.description: New Bialla police barracks houses now ready for occupation (NBC News) Police officers in the Nakanai district of West New Britain Province have received a boost to their living conditions with the commissioning of the new Bialla police barracks on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
New Bialla police barracks houses now ready for occupation (NBC News)

Police officers in the Nakanai district of West New Britain Province have received a boost to their living conditions with the commissioning of the new Bialla police barracks on Wednesday.

The new barracks, comprised of 14 houses was built at a total cost of K9.6 million using tax credits from the major Oil Palm milling company operating in the area-Hargy Oil Palms Limited.

Nakanai MP, Francis Galia Maneke, Governor Sasindran Muthuvel and Deputy Commissioner for Police-Administration, Dr.Philip Mitna jointly opened the new barracks.

Minister Maneke acknowledged Hargy Oil Palms Limited for fulfilling its community service obligations through the usage of its tax credits to build the barracks.

He said the company continues to partner well with the government to serve the people of East Nakanai and this project is a demonstration of this partnership.

Maneke highlighted that law and order and criminal activities continue to pose a major challenge for the authorities and the new facilities will now ensure that more police personnel can be stationed in Bialla and maintain the rule of law.

Meanwhile, Governor Muthuvel also shared similar sentiments in acknowledging the partnership with Hargy Oil Palms Limited.

"Today is not simply about opening 14 houses. It is about strengthening our police force, improving the welfare of our officers and investing in law and order, which is fundamental to development,

"On behalf of the people and Government of West New Britain, I sincerely congratulate and thank Hargy Oil Palms for delivering this important project.

"We are opening 14 quality police houses, fully fenced, with a total investment of approximately K10 million. These are well-designed, quality facilities. In fact, I must honestly say that the standard of these houses is very impressive. They are even better than some of the 18 plus 2 houses that we have managed to construct in Kimbe using our limited provincial resources," Governor Muthuvel clarified.

item.title: El Nino drives Island communities into gold panning for survival
item.description: Woodlark mining workers with water carts assisting locals at Kulumwadau ward (Supplied) ‎People on Woodlark Island in the Samarai -Murua district, Milne Bay Province, say their crops are now turning into roasted food in their gardens in this El Nino' period, threatening their food security.
item.content:encoded:
Woodlark mining workers with water carts assisting locals at Kulumwadau ward (Supplied)

‎People on Woodlark Island in the Samarai -Murua district, Milne Bay Province, say their crops are now turning into roasted food in their gardens in this El Nino' period, threatening their food security.

‎In Kulumwadau ward on the western part of Woodlark Island, residents are now depending entirely on alluvial gold panning as the main means of survival daily with their families.

‎With food gardens drying up under this El Nino induced weather, gold panning has become a daily survival activity for families in Kulumwadau ward.

Ward councilor, Ephraim Waiyaki tells us from the island, residents are dependent on their gold dust obtained from panning, which they exchange for food supplies at local trade stores.

‎He says the Ward Development Committee (WDC) has urged local business houses to maintain adequate stock to meet the growing demand of food on the island.

"Panning is the main source of income that enables families to buy food from stores.

‎"Ward Development Committee (WDC) has advised business houses to maintain their stocks. WDC has also cut down on ward work parades to allow people to pan gold as a survival measure," councilor Waiyaki said.

‎Meanwhile, Woodlark Mining has stepped in to assist with the community's water needs by using water carts to refill household tanks.

‎Water is collected from nearby creeks and transported by mines water carts to homes within Kulumwadau ward.

item.title: EU Ambassador visits Binatang research centre in Madang
item.description: EU Ambassador to PNG, Her Excellency Erika Hasznos paying a courtesy visit to Madang’s Provincial Administrator Daniel Aloi yesterday (Supplied-EU media) The EU Ambassador to Papua New Guinea, Her Excellency Erika Hasznos, is impressed with the work of Madang- based Binatang Research Centre.
item.content:encoded:
EU Ambassador to PNG, Her Excellency Erika Hasznos paying a courtesy visit to Madang’s Provincial Administrator Daniel Aloi yesterday (Supplied-EU media)

The EU Ambassador to Papua New Guinea, Her Excellency Erika Hasznos, is impressed with the work of Madang- based Binatang Research Centre.

The New Guinea Binatang Research Centre is a biological research and conservation NGO in the country.

Her Excellency Hasznos arrived in Madang yesterday on a two- day visit to the centre where EU is sponsoring 42 students who are currently doing various research works on biodiversity, forestry and climate change.

She said, "The purpose of my visit is to see the project that European Union is funding in Madang. This project is related to forestry, climate change and biodiversity, which is very important here in Papua New Guinea.

"The overall value of this project is more than K220 million, and it focuses on education and young people."

The EU Ambassador took a tour of the research facility at Nagada, outside town, and was impressed with what she saw.

"We would like to empower future environmental leaders of Papua New Guinea because we believe that environmental protection can be built from the bottom. It can be built with young people engaging in education and research, and protecting the environment, the very valuable biodiversity, rainforest, and all the natural aspects, here in Madang and also around Papua New Guinea," she said.

The Madang project focuses on the scholarship of the 42 scholarships for young PNG students who are engaged in Masters studies, in PhD studies and research works.

They are all working in different environmental and biodiversity areas.

"They are also working in partnership with European universities, with researchers from other countries, and together they are making very big contributions to the conservation of the biodiversity of the country," Ambassador Hasznos added.

She was also amazed with the work that the New Guinea Binatang Research Centre is doing in the area of research, conservation and training of young people.

Her Excellency Hasznos said, "I am very impressed with what we've seen so far. We've met alot of scholarship students who are studying under the EU- funding program, we've met several lecturers, researches, and they have also shown us how the Binatang Research Centre is connected to this project, and what it is doing to preserving and also researching the biodiversity of Papua New Guinea.

"We've also seen an enormous amount of species that the centre has already categorised, and how this these educational networks are building students from Madang, Papua New Guinea and also from Europe," the EU Ambassador stated.

Her Excellency Hasznos is also the Head of the European Union delegation to Papua New Guinea.

Today, she will be witnessing the graduation of 21 scholars who have attended a biological course.

The scholars were also taken on field trips and training in the night at Wanang Swire Conservation Station.

They also went for an Ecological field trip to Manam Island last week.
